title: Bypasses for Z-Tunnel 2.0: VPN gateway bypasses, destination exclusions and inclusions, domain bypasses

checks.do: For a destination tunneled despite an exclusion: list every inclusion and exclusion that covers it and apply the specificity order (netmask, then number of fields, then inclusion wins); also check VPN gateway bypasses, which come first.
For a migrated tenant: whether network bypasses still sit in the app profile PAC instead of VPN gateway bypasses or destination exclusions.
For a domain bypass on Windows: the client version, and on 3.8+ both listening proxy options and whether the request matched the app profile PAC's default return.
For a VPN gateway entered as an FQDN: whether its current IP was in the bypass list resolved at tunnel start.

pac-not-for-2.statement: For Z-Tunnel 1.0, network bypasses can go in the app profile PAC file; for Z-Tunnel 2.0 the vendor says not to put them there and to add them as VPN gateway bypasses or destination exclusions.

quotes: For Z-Tunnel 1.0, you can add network bypasses to the app profile PAC file. But if you are using Z-Tunnel 2.0, do not add network bypasses to the Zscaler Client Connector profile policy’s PAC file. For Z-Tunnel 2.0, you must add the network bypasses as VPN gateway bypasses or destination exclusions.

vpn-gateway-bypass.statement: VPN gateway bypasses take IPs, subnets or FQDNs, create routes and filters that send traffic direct, and have the highest priority over all other bypass types; the system sets a filter so the app does not need to process the bypassed traffic.

quotes: VPN Gateway bypasses allow you to create routes and filters for direct traffic. You can use IPs, subnets, or FQDNs. This type of bypass has the highest priority over all other bypass types.
When you create a VPN gateway bypass, the system sets a filter to ignore VPN traffic without Zscaler Client Connector needing to process the bypass.

vpn-gateway-mechanism.statement: With the route-based driver the app creates exclude routes in the routing table for these bypasses; with the filter-based driver it creates bypass filters.

quotes: When a route-based driver is in use, the app creates IP-based exclude routes in the routing table. When a filter-based driver is in use, it creates bypass filters in the filter table.
evidence.after: To add a new Windows policy rule:

vpn-gateway-fqdn.statement: An FQDN bypass is resolved by the client and its addresses are added at the start of the tunnel, so an address it resolves to later might not be bypassed; the app resolves all entries again after a network change, many FQDNs slow tunnel startup, and the vendor prefers IPs or subnets.

quotes: If you add a fully qualified domain name (FQDN), the FQDN resolves and all resulting IP addresses are added to the bypass list at the start of the tunnel. However, if the FQDN resolves to a different IP address later, that address might not be bypassed.
Adding too many FQDNs can slow tunnel startup because Zscaler Client Connector resolves all these domains before starting tunneling.

While you can also use this field to bypass non-VPN destinations, you must limit the number of items in this list because Zscaler Client Connector attempts to resolve all entries after a network change.
Zscaler recommends adding an IP or subnet where possible.
evidence.after: To add a new Windows policy rule:

quotes: For every hostname entered, a DNS resolution is performed by the client.

vpn-gateway-required.statement: When users run a VPN client alongside Client Connector, a VPN gateway bypass is required if Tunnel is the forwarding action for any trusted network type, or if the VPN runs in split-tunnel mode.

quotes: When your users have a VPN client running on their devices in conjunction with Zscaler Client Connector, the VPN gateway bypass must be used in these scenarios:
You selected Tunnel for the forwarding profile action of any trusted network type.
Your VPN runs in Split-Tunnel mode so that it takes some, but not all, user traffic from the device.
evidence.after: To add a new Windows policy rule:

incl-excl-patterns.statement: Destination exclusions and inclusions in the app profile select which traffic Z-Tunnel 2.0 sends to the Public Service Edge; the vendor recommends either 0.0.0.0/0 in exclusions with specific subnets included, or 0.0.0.0/0 in inclusions with specific subnets excluded.

quotes: Include specific subnets only by adding 0.0.0.0/0 to Destination Exclusions and entering specific subnets to the Destination Inclusions.
Exclude specific subnets only by adding 0.0.0.0/0 to Destination Inclusions and entering specific subnets to the Destination Exclusions.

You can add specific subnets to the Destination Exclusions and Destination Inclusion fields in the Zscaler Client Connector app profile, allowing you to send a specific subset of your traffic to the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS through Z-Tunnel 2.0.

conflict-resolution.statement: When an exclusion and an inclusion conflict, Z-Tunnel 2.0 picks the rule with the more specific netmask; with equal netmasks, the rule with more fields (ports, port ranges, protocols); and with identical rules, the inclusion. The app profile help gives the case of 192.0.2.0/24 included and 192.0.2.0/24:*:tcp excluded: TCP to that subnet bypasses Z-Tunnel 2.0.

quotes: Z-Tunnel 2.0 chooses the rule with the more specific netmask. For example, 10.0.0.0/24 is chosen over 10.0.0.0/16.
If the subnet mask is the same, Z-Tunnel 2.0 chooses the rule with the highest number of fields (therefore more specific), after taking all ports, port ranges, and protocols into account.
If the exclusions and inclusions rules are identical, Z-Tunnel 2.0 chooses the inclusions.

If you enter overlapping values in the inclusion and exclusion lists, the longest match takes precedence (e.g., if 192.0.2.0/24 is in IPv4 Inclusion and 192.0.2.0/24:*:tcp is in IPv4 Exclusion, any TCP requests to the 192.0.2.0/24 subnet bypass Z-Tunnel 2.0.
evidence.after: To add a new Windows policy rule:

port-bypass.statement: Port-based bypasses work only on Windows and macOS: the port or port range is appended to a destination exclusion, as in 192.168.1/24:80 or 192.168.1/24:80-85.

quotes: Configuring port-based bypasses is only possible for Windows and macOS.
The port-based bypass is 192.168.1/24:80.
The port-based bypass is 192.168.1/24:80-85.

bypass-scope.statement: These IP bypasses and inclusions need a forwarding profile with Z-Tunnel 2.0 selected, and apply to Z-Tunnel 1.0 only when a device configured for Z-Tunnel 2.0 is falling back to 1.0.

quotes: You must choose a forwarding profile with Z-Tunnel 2.0 selected. These bypasses apply to Z-Tunnel 1.0 only if the device is configured for Z-Tunnel 2.0 and is falling back to Z-Tunnel 1.0.
evidence.after: To add a new Windows policy rule:

process-bypass.statement: Process-Based Application Bypass in the app profile bypasses applications defined by process in Application Bypass, for both Z-Tunnel 1.0 and 2.0.

quotes: Process-Based Application Bypass: Allows bypassing of process-based applications created in Application Bypass that you can use for both Z-Tunnel 1.0 and Z-Tunnel 2.0.
evidence.after: To add a new Windows policy rule:

domain-needs-listener.statement: Domain-based bypasses, for applications that do not resolve to a single IP, use PAC files and need the Z-Tunnel 1.0 listener, which can bypass only web (HTTP and HTTPS) traffic coming from the system proxy: system proxy traffic is routed to the listener and the domains are bypassed in the app profile PAC.

quotes: This bypass requires Z-Tunnel 1.0 listener, which can only bypass the web traffic (i.e., HTTP/HTTPS traffic) originating from the system proxy. You must route system proxy traffic to the listener and then bypass the domains in the app profile PAC.
This allows you to create bypasses for domain-based applications (i.e., applications that can’t be resolved to a single IP address).

dual-pac.statement: On Windows 3.7 and earlier, a domain bypass needs two PAC files: the forwarding profile PAC returns `PROXY ${ZAPP_TUNNEL2_BYPASS}` for the domain (the vendor's example then falls through to DIRECT for all other traffic, which its comment says tunnels using Tunnel2), and the app profile PAC returns DIRECT for the same domain.

evidence.after: For Zscaler Client Connector Version 3.7 and Earlier for Windows
quotes: Configure the forwarding profile PAC file to include the Z-Tunnel 2.0 bypass return statement for any destinations you want to send directly.

function FindProxyForURL(url, host) { /* Updates are directly accessible */ if (dnsDomainIs(host, "<domain>")) return "PROXY ${ZAPP_TUNNEL2_BYPASS}"; /* Default Traffic Forwarding. Return DIRECT to tunnel using Tunnel2 */ return "DIRECT"; }
Configure the app profile PAC file to include a return direct statement for the domain:

fp-pac-scope.statement: In Tunnel mode the forwarding profile PAC may only bypass traffic away from Client Connector or send it to Client Connector, never tunnel it to the Zscaler cloud.

quotes: In Tunnel mode, you must only use the forwarding profile PAC file to bypass traffic away from Zscaler Client Connector or to tunnel traffic to Zscaler Client Connector. Do not use it to tunnel traffic to the Zscaler cloud.

pac-wildcards.statement: In these PAC functions a leading period is a wildcard in `dnsDomainIs` (".domain.com") and a leading asterisk is a wildcard in `shExpMatch` ("*.domain.com").

quotes: In this example, a leading period (.) is treated as a wildcard in this function: (dnsDomainIs(host, ".domain.com"))
In this example, a leading asterisk (*) is treated as a wildcard in the function: (shExpMatch(host,"*.domain.com"))

redirect-web.statement: On Windows 3.8 and later, Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy sends TCP 80 and 443 to the listening proxy and the rest through Z-Tunnel 2.0, so app profile PAC bypasses apply to web traffic without a forwarding profile PAC.

quotes: For Zscaler Client Connector version 3.8 and later for Windows, you can enable Forwarding Profile options that don’t require configuring a system proxy PAC in the forwarding profile.

Select Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy to split traffic so that the TCP port 80 and TCP port 443 traffic go to the Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy, with the remaining traffic passing through Z-Tunnel 2.0.
By using this option, bypasses in the app profile PAC can be applied to web traffic without a forwarding profile PAC.

bypasses-before-listener.statement: Z-Tunnel 2.0 inclusions and exclusions and VPN hostname bypasses are applied before traffic is sent to the listening proxy, so when Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy is enabled, only TCP 80 and 443 traffic covered by the inclusions reaches it.

quotes: Z-Tunnel 2.0 inclusions and exclusions and VPN hostname bypasses are applied before sending traffic to the listening proxy. Hence, only the TCP 80/443 traffic covered by the Z-Tunnel 2.0 inclusions is sent to the listening proxy when this option is enabled.

Select Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy to split traffic so that the TCP port 80 and TCP port 443 traffic go to the Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy, with the remaining traffic passing through Z-Tunnel 2.0.

use-t2-proxied.statement: Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic makes the app carry web traffic received on the listening proxy over Z-Tunnel 2.0; with it off and the redirect on, web traffic uses Z-Tunnel 1.0 and the rest Z-Tunnel 2.0.

quotes: Select Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic to have Zscaler Client Connector use the Z-Tunnel 2.0 protocol to tunnel web traffic received on the Zscaler Client Connector listening proxy.

If this option is disabled and Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy is enabled, Zscaler Client Connector uses Z-Tunnel 1.0 for web traffic and Z-Tunnel 2.0 for the remaining system traffic.

use-t2-default-only.statement: That option applies only to connections that match the app profile PAC's default return statement; a request matching a statement that sends traffic to a specific Public Service Edge ignores it and uses Z-Tunnel 1.0.

quotes: Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic is applied to connections arriving on the Zscaler Client Connector listening proxy only if they match the default return statement in the app profile PAC.

If the request matches a particular statement in the app profile PAC that redirects traffic to a specific Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS, then this option is ignored and traffic is sent using Z-Tunnel 1.0.

recommend-both.statement: Zscaler recommends enabling both Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy and Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic.

quotes: Zscaler recommends enabling both Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy and Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic.

listening-proxy-table.statement: The vendor's table for the two options: redirect on and Z-Tunnel 2.0 for proxied traffic off sends web traffic to the listening proxy through Z-Tunnel 1.0; redirect off and the option on sends system-proxy web traffic (such as 127.0.0.1:9000) through the listening proxy to Z-Tunnel 2.0 and other web traffic straight to Z-Tunnel 2.0; both on sends web traffic to the listening proxy through Z-Tunnel 2.0. Non-web traffic goes to Z-Tunnel 2.0 in every case.

quotes: | Redirect Web Traffic to Zscaler Client Connector Listening Proxy option | Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for Proxied Web Traffic option | Web Traffic | Non-Web Traffic |
| Enabled | Disabled | Forward to the listening proxy through Z-Tunnel 1.0 | Send directly to Z-Tunnel 2.0 |

| Disabled | Enabled | If using a system proxy (like 127.0.0.1:9000), forward to the Zscaler listening proxy and then send to Z-Tunnel 2.0.If not using a system proxy, send directly to Z-Tunnel 2.0. | Send directly to Z-Tunnel 2.0 |
| Enabled | Enabled | Forward to the listening proxy through Z-Tunnel 2.0. | Send directly to Z-Tunnel 2.0 |

pac-bypass-effect.title: What network bypasses left in the app profile PAC do under Z-Tunnel 2.0
pac-bypass-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Z-Tunnel 2.0 ignores PAC-based network bypasses ... An operator migrating a 1.0 deployment to 2.0 by copying PAC bypasses gets no bypass effect on 2.0 traffic." The vendor only says not to put them there. With the listening proxy redirect on, app profile PAC bypasses do apply to web traffic, so "ignored" cannot be right in every configuration.
pac-bypass-effect.blocks: explaining a bypass that works for web traffic and not for other traffic after migration

process-bypass-precedence.title: How process-based bypass ranks against destination inclusions
process-bypass-precedence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: process-based Application Bypass "matches specific process names / executables and bypasses them regardless of Destination Exclusions config". The help says it works for both tunnel versions but gives no order against inclusions and exclusions.

mobile-push.title: Whether push notifications (APNs, FCM) need destination exclusions on mobile Client Connector
mobile-push.detail: Unverified legacy statement: push-MFA apps such as Duo, Microsoft Authenticator and Okta Verify fail on Wi-Fi behind the tunnel unless Apple Push (17.0.0.0/8, TCP 443 and 5223) and Firebase Cloud Messaging (fcm.googleapis.com, play.googleapis.com, TCP 443) are excluded; iOS allows one VPN profile at a time. The legacy doc cited Apple and Duo pages that are not registered sources, and no Zscaler page in the captures states it.
